name: Australian King Parrot
habitat: Wet forests, rainforest edges, well-treed gardens
call_description: High-pitched piping whistle in flight; rolling "carr-ack"
fun_fact: Males are the only Australian parrots with a completely red head.
appearance: Male has scarlet head and underparts with green wings; female has a green head and breast with a red belly.

name: Australian Magpie
habitat: Open woodland, parks, gardens, farmland
call_description: Rich, melodious carolling, especially at dawn
fun_fact: Can recognise and remember individual human faces for years.
appearance: Bold black-and-white bird with a white nape and shoulders, red-brown eyes and a sturdy blue-white bill.

name: Australian Raven
habitat: Woodland, farmland, urban areas
diet: Insects, carrion, grain, refuse, small animals
call_description: Long, wailing "aah-aah-aaaahh" fading at the end
fun_fact: Its drawn-out death-wail call distinguishes it from other corvids.
appearance: Large all-black bird with a heavy bill, white eyes and prominent throat hackles.

name: Black-faced Cuckoo-shrike
habitat: Open forests, woodlands, parks and gardens
fun_fact: Often shuffles and refolds its wings on landing, earning the nickname "shufflewing".
appearance: Sleek blue-grey bird with a jet-black face and throat and a gently undulating flight.

name: Common Blackbird
habitat: Urban gardens, parks, orchards (introduced)
call_description: Rich, mellow fluting song, often at dusk
fun_fact: Introduced from Europe in the 1850s; males sing from high perches at dawn and dusk.
appearance: Male is all black with a bright orange-yellow bill and eye-ring; female is dark brown with a mottled breast.

name: Common Myna
habitat: Urban areas, farmland (introduced)
fun_fact: Roosts communally in groups of up to several thousand birds.
appearance: Chocolate-brown body with a glossy black head, yellow bill, legs and bare yellow skin behind the eye; white wing patches flash in flight.

name: Crested Pigeon
habitat: Open woodland, parks, sports fields, roadsides
call_description: Distinctive whistling wingbeat on take-off; soft "whoop"
fun_fact: The whistling sound in flight is made by air rushing over a modified wing feather.
appearance: Grey pigeon with a thin upright black crest, pinkish flanks and iridescent bronze wing patches barred with black.

name: Crimson Rosella
habitat: Wet forests, mountain woodlands, leafy gardens
fun_fact: Young birds are largely green and gradually turn crimson over 15 months.
appearance: Rich crimson body with bright blue cheeks, blue wings and tail, and black-scalloped back feathers.

name: Eastern Spinebill
habitat: Heathland, forests, gardens with tubular flowers
fun_fact: Can hover briefly while feeding on nectar, much like a hummingbird.
appearance: Tiny honeyeater with a long, fine down-curved bill, cinnamon underparts, white throat patch and black head band.

name: Eastern Yellow Robin
habitat: Wet forests, woodland understorey, shaded gullies
call_description: Repeated piping "chop chop"; bell-like notes at dawn
fun_fact: Often perches sideways on tree trunks, scanning the ground for prey.
appearance: Grey-backed robin with a bright yellow breast and belly and a pale grey throat; upright, confiding posture.

name: Galah
habitat: Open grasslands, farmland, urban parks
fun_fact: Pairs bond for life, and flocks perform spectacular acrobatics in windy weather.
appearance: Rose-pink face and underparts with soft grey back and wings and a pale pink crest.

name: Grey Butcherbird
habitat: Woodlands, urban parks and gardens
call_description: Beautiful rollicking, piping song, often in duet
fun_fact: Wedges surplus prey into tree forks — a habit that earned the family its name.
appearance: Grey back with black head, white collar and underparts, and a hooked, silver-grey bill with a black tip.

name: Grey Fantail
habitat: Forests, woodlands, gardens — almost anywhere with trees
fun_fact: Almost never sits still — it fans its tail and pirouettes constantly to flush insects.
appearance: Small grey bird with a white eyebrow and throat, buff belly, and a long tail fanned wide and swung from side to side.

name: House Sparrow
habitat: Urban areas, farms (introduced)
fun_fact: One of the world's most widespread birds, introduced to Australia in the 1860s.
appearance: Male has a grey crown, black bib and chestnut nape; female is plain grey-brown with a pale eyebrow.

name: Koel
habitat: Tall trees in suburbs, rainforest edges (spring–summer migrant)
call_description: Loud, rising "koo-ell" repeated endlessly, often at night
fun_fact: A brood parasite — it lays its eggs in the nests of wattlebirds and friarbirds.
appearance: Male is glossy blue-black with a red eye; female is brown with white spots and heavy barring below.

name: Laughing Kookaburra
habitat: Open forests, woodlands, parks with old trees
diet: Insects, lizards, snakes, rodents, small birds
call_description: Famous raucous laughing chorus at dawn and dusk
fun_fact: The world's largest kingfisher, and its "laugh" is a territorial claim, not amusement.
appearance: Stocky bird with a huge bill, whitish head and underparts, brown eye-stripe and back, and blue-flecked wings.

name: Little Wattlebird
habitat: Banksia heathland, coastal scrub, gardens
fun_fact: Despite the name, it lacks the neck wattles of other wattlebirds.
appearance: Grey-brown honeyeater heavily streaked with white, with rufous wing patches visible in flight and a blue-grey eye.

name: Magpie-lark
habitat: Open areas near water, urban lawns, parks
call_description: Metallic "pee-wee" duet sung in perfect alternation
fun_fact: Pairs sing precisely-timed duets — each bird contributes alternate notes.
appearance: Neat black-and-white bird smaller than a magpie; male has a black throat and white eyebrow, female a white face and throat.

name: New Holland Honeyeater
habitat: Heathland, banksia scrub, flowering gardens
fun_fact: Among the first Australian birds scientifically described, back in 1790.
appearance: Striking black-and-white streaked honeyeater with large yellow wing panels, yellow tail edges and a white eye.

name: Noisy Miner
habitat: Open woodland, urban parks and gardens
call_description: Constant piping alarm calls and chattering
fun_fact: Lives in aggressive colonies that mob intruders and drive smaller birds away.
appearance: Grey honeyeater with a black crown and cheeks, yellow bill, yellow bare skin behind the eye and yellow legs.

name: Pied Butcherbird
habitat: Open woodland, farmland with scattered trees
call_description: Superb flute-like caroling, often at night
fun_fact: Widely considered one of the finest songbirds in the world.
appearance: Crisp black hood and bib over white collar and underparts, black back with white wing stripes and rump.

name: Pied Currawong
habitat: Forests and woodlands; urban areas in winter
fun_fact: Named for its call; mountain populations move into lowland towns each winter.
appearance: Large black bird with bright yellow eyes and bold white patches on wings, rump and tail tip.

name: Purple Swamphen
habitat: Wetlands, reed beds, lake edges, urban ponds
diet: Reed shoots, aquatic plants, frogs, eggs
fun_fact: Holds food in one long-toed foot like a hand while eating.
appearance: Large deep-blue waterbird with a heavy red bill and frontal shield, red legs and a flicking white undertail.

name: Rainbow Lorikeet
habitat: Coastal forests, urban gardens with flowering trees
fun_fact: Its brush-tipped tongue is specialised for harvesting nectar and pollen.
appearance: Unmistakable: deep blue head and belly, bright green wings, orange-red breast and a red bill.

name: Red Wattlebird
habitat: Open forests, gardens with nectar plants
call_description: Harsh coughing bark and gurgling chatter
fun_fact: One of Australia's largest honeyeaters, named for its red neck wattles.
appearance: Big streaked grey-brown honeyeater with red eye-wattles, a yellow belly and white facial streaks.

name: Red-browed Finch
habitat: Grassy areas near dense cover, creek edges, gardens
fun_fact: Travels in bouncing flocks that "explode" into cover when startled.
appearance: Small olive-and-grey finch with a bright red eyebrow, rump and bill.

name: Red-whiskered Bulbul
habitat: Suburban gardens, parks (introduced)
fun_fact: Native to Asia; established around Sydney and Melbourne from cage-bird releases in the 1880s.
appearance: Jaunty brown bird with a tall black crest, red cheek-whisker patch, white underparts and a red vent.

name: Rock Dove
habitat: Cities, towns, bridges, grain stores (introduced)
fun_fact: The familiar city pigeon — descended from cliff-nesting doves domesticated over 5,000 years ago.
appearance: Typically blue-grey with two black wing bars and iridescent green-purple neck sheen, though plumage varies widely.

name: Silvereye
habitat: Almost any shrubby habitat: forests, heath, gardens, orchards
call_description: Soft warbling song; thin "psee" contact calls
fun_fact: Tasmanian silvereyes migrate over Bass Strait to the mainland each winter.
appearance: Tiny olive-green bird with a conspicuous ring of white feathers around each eye and a grey back.

name: Spotted Pardalote
habitat: Eucalypt forest canopy; nests in earth-bank tunnels
diet: Lerps, scale insects, other tiny invertebrates
fun_fact: One of Australia's smallest birds — it digs a nesting tunnel up to 1 m into earthen banks.
appearance: Jewel-like: black wings, head and tail sprinkled with white spots, yellow throat and a red rump.

name: Spotted Turtle-dove
habitat: Urban gardens, parks, farmland (introduced)
fun_fact: Introduced from Asia in the 1860s; the "spotted" collar is absent in young birds.
appearance: Soft grey-brown dove with a black nape collar finely spotted with white.

name: Sulphur-crested Cockatoo
habitat: Forests, woodlands, urban parks
call_description: Ear-splitting harsh screech, especially at roosts
fun_fact: Can live for more than 80 years and posts "sentinel" birds while the flock feeds.
appearance: Large white cockatoo with an expressive sulphur-yellow crest and a pale yellow wash under wings and tail.

name: Superb Fairy-wren
habitat: Dense shrubs bordering open grassy areas, gardens
fun_fact: Breeding males present yellow flower petals to females during courtship.
appearance: Breeding male has an iridescent sky-blue crown, cheeks and back with a black mask; females and non-breeders are plain brown with a reddish eye-ring.

name: Welcome Swallow
habitat: Open country near water; nests on buildings and bridges
diet: Flying insects caught on the wing
fun_fact: Named because its arrival signalled the coming of spring to early settlers.
appearance: Graceful swallow with glossy blue-black upperparts, rusty forehead and throat, and a deeply forked tail.

name: Willie Wagtail
habitat: Open areas, lawns, paddocks — nearly Australia-wide
diet: Insects caught on the ground or in the air
fun_fact: Fearlessly harasses eagles and kookaburras many times its size.
appearance: Black above and white below with white eyebrows it raises and lowers to signal mood; wags its fanned tail restlessly.

name: Yellow-tailed Black Cockatoo
habitat: Eucalypt forest, pine plantations, coastal heath
diet: Wood-boring grubs, banksia and pine seeds
fun_fact: Tears open tree trunks with its massive bill to extract wood-boring grubs.
appearance: Huge dusky-black cockatoo with pale feather edging, yellow cheek patches and broad yellow tail panels.
